review.subject: Cellwork: cross-cell answer visibility, stable seat keys, acknowledgement refusal reasons
review.contract: .mpd/plans/mail-unify.md §6 (R4's findings), with T17's workspace-wide references as the other half of the cross-cell fix
review.sandwich: All cellwork hashes were identical at gate start (11:12:37Z) and review end (11:14:50Z). No other writer touched the package during this review.

verdict.justification: All three R4 findings are closed end-to-end by my own tool-level probes: a reseeded seat acknowledges the rows addressed to its stable seat key exactly once and answers its seat-key question; a pre-fix row still cannot be acknowledged, but the refusal is now CARRIED and RENDERED with the store's reason; and a cross-cell question is answered in BOTH directions without an explicit questionId, with the parent inbox holding the echoed labels. 182/182 tests, 6/6 gates green. One non-blocking Nit on the migration refusal's wording.

findingsAudit.finding: F1 (R4 High, layer 1) — a cross-cell structured ANSWER could not round-trip: the question's key was resolved from the TARGET cell's view
findingsAudit.evidence: protocol.ts resolves the answered row with `findWorkspaceMailById(workspace, replyTo)` first and the target view as the legacy fallback; the refusals now name the real defect. Probes: F1 (parent→sub question, sub→parent answer WITHOUT questionId → ok; sub sees the question, parent's inbox holds selected ['A. unify']; the REVERSE direction also ok) and F1c ('names no message in this workspace's mailbox' / 'names a "message" row with no question payload', not the old missing-key wording). The T18 arm covers both directions too.

findingsAudit.finding: F2 (R4 Medium) — a seat's address was its session id at send time, so a reseeded/never-raised seat could never ack its mail or answer its question
findingsAudit.evidence: `seatKey(cell,name) = "seat:<cellId>/<nameKey>"` is the address (`seatAddress`) AND the send identity (`fromId: seatKey(cell, caller.member)`) AND the ack identity (`byId: seatKey(caller.cell, seat)`). Probes: F2 a row addressed to the seat key is acknowledged exactly once by a reseeded session (first acked 1, refused [], second 0); F2b the reseeded seat answers the seat-key question (ok). The shipped T18 arm ('a reseeded seat acknowledges … and answers it') matches.

findingsAudit.finding: N1 (R4 Nit) — an ownership refusal during the inbox ack was invisible (`acknowledged: 0`, no reason)
findingsAudit.evidence: `acknowledgeCellMail` now uses `acknowledge` (not the moved-only wrapper) and returns `refused: [{id, reason}]`; the tool returns it and the RENDER prints 'acknowledgement refused for N row(s), which stay unread: …'. Probe N1 (a pre-fix session-addressed row): acknowledged 0, refused[0].id = the row, reason = 'only its recipient may acknowledge it', and the rendered text carries it. The shipped arm asserts the same including the render.

regression.item: same-cell question/answer + broadcast + legacy ack-once + member-to-member
regression.result: PASS — 182/182 in the package, the four B9/C2.2/C2.3/D6 arms and the mail-order suite green; my R1 probe shows member-to-member durable + the preserved wake sentence.
PASS — probe R2: the checkpoint refusal still names both tools and states a structured question cannot be asked/answered at a checkpoint.

KNOWN BOUND, not charged to T18: probe F1b shows a NON-recipient seat can still 'answer' the cross-cell question because the store's ownership lookup is team-scoped (T19's F2). T18's design is COMPATIBLE with the fix (the legitimate answerer's `fromId` = the question's `toId` seat key), so the T17 repair must not break it.

findings.title: The refusal sentence for a pre-fix (session-addressed) row reads circularly: the addressee name and the caller name are identical
findings.where: packages/mpd-team-core-plugin/src/mailbox-store.ts · acknowledge's refusal sentence, surfaced by the cellwork inbox
findings.what: Probe N1's reason: 'mail-prefix-row was addressed to "cell-planner", not to "cell-planner" — only its recipient may acknowledge it'. The stored `toName` is the seat name and the caller's `byName` is the same seat name, so the sentence names the same person twice and does not reveal that the TO ID differed (a pre-fix session id vs the stable seat key).
findings.why: The whole point of N1's fix is a diagnosable reason; for the migration case the sentence is legible only if the reader already knows the old addressing scheme. Low impact (the row id and the rule are correct).
findings.direction: Include the ids or a short parenthetical in the refusal (e.g. 'addressed to seat "…" via "<toId>"'), or phrase the migration case as 'the row predates the stable seat key'. Optional.
